relationships.subject: Ift88
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal administration of siRNA targeting Ift88, a primary cilium-specific intraflagellar transport (IFT) protein required for ciliary integrity, resulted in attenuation of Ift88 mRNA and nociceptor primary cilia.

relationships.subject: nociceptor primary cilium
relationships.evidence_quote: Attenuation of primary cilia was associated with an increase in mechanical nociceptive threshold in vivo and decrease in nociceptor excitability in vitro

relationships.subject: PGE2
relationships.evidence_quote: Treatment of rats with Ift88 siRNA markedly attenuated the mechanical hyperalgesia induced by PGE2.

relationships.subject: paclitaxel
relationships.evidence_quote: we also evaluated whether CIPN, induced by a chemotherapy drug, paclitaxel, is primary cilium dependent

relationships.subject: Ift88
relationships.evidence_quote: In support of this hypothesis, we found that siRNA targeting Ift88 markedly attenuates CIPN.

relationships.subject: Ift52
relationships.evidence_quote: As observed following treatment with Ift88 siRNA, Ift52 siRNA also markedly attenuated paclitaxel CIPN.

relationships.subject: cyclopamine
relationships.evidence_quote: Administration of cyclopamine, by both routes of administration, attenuated paclitaxel-induced hyperalgesia

relationships.subject: Sonic hedgehog
relationships.evidence_quote: Treatment of rats with Ift88 siRNA reduced the hyperalgesia induced by both intradermal and intraganglion Shh

key_findings: Rat nociceptors bear primary cilia; intrathecal Ift88 siRNA reduced cilia, raised mechanical threshold and rheobase, and attenuated PGE2 hyperalgesia and paclitaxel CIPN in males but not females.
Shh-induced hyperalgesia depended on primary cilia, and the Hedgehog inhibitor cyclopamine attenuated established paclitaxel CIPN.
